english.title: Supply classified video other than in licensed sex shop
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), supplied a classified video recording containing a video work, namely **(..SPECIFY THE TITLE OF THE VIDEO RECORDING..), in respect of which the classification certificate issued did not allow for that work to be supplied other than in a licensed sex shop, at a place, namely **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..), for which a licence under Schedule 3 to the Local Government (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1982 was not in force
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12(1) and (4A) of the Video Recordings Act 1984.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Time limit for prosecution - either within three years of the commission of the offence of within one year of its discovery by the prosecutor, whichever is the earlier (Section 15(1)).(ii) See Section 11(1) and (2) for exemptions and defences and Sections 2 and 3 for definitions of 'exempted work' and 'exempted supply'.
(iii) See also Section 14A for general defences.
(iv) See Sections 16A and 16B for extended powers of enforcing authorities and extended jurisdiction of magistrates' courts.
(v) See offence wording H3707 for possessing classified video recording intended for supply other than in a licensed sex shop.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
